headline: HSBC is planning deep job cuts in its UK wealth management business, including about half of management and specialist roles, as it brings in more AI, the Financial Times reports.
score_reason: Single-source report from unnamed people; the bank has not confirmed the figures.
importance_line: Financial advisers and specialist staff in HSBC's UK wealth arm face the deepest cuts, but the figures come from unnamed sources and the plan is still in consultation.
summary: The Financial Times reported, as relayed by Reuters and citing people familiar with the plans, that HSBC wants to cut about half of management and specialist roles in its UK wealth business, with reductions among financial advisers that could reach around 70%. Affected staff are expected to leave by the end of the month while a consultation is under way; HSBC's statement to Reuters speaks of more digitally enabled products and gives no figures, and CEO Georges Elhedery said in May that 'generative AI will destroy certain jobs'.
